# Receita test fixture

`Empresas.csv`, `Estabelecimentos.csv` and `Socios.csv` follow the real
format of the Receita CNPJ files (see `docs/sources/receita.md`): no header,
`;` between fields, every field in double quotes, LF line ends, **Latin-1**
encoding. Tests zip each one on the fly (`Empresas0.zip` with entry
`Empresas.csv`, and so on), like the published files.

**All personal data is synthetic.** Every person name and CPF fragment was
invented; companies named after people (the sole proprietor) are invented
too. Apart from Banco do Brasil, every CNPJ base starts with `9899` (or is the
alphanumeric `98AB0001`), a range with no company in the 2026-10 files, so no
real company is attached to invented partners. Banco do Brasil (`00000000`,
a large public company) keeps its real registry row and has no partners here.

The files are marked `binary` in `.gitattributes`: git must not rewrite their
encoding or line ends. Line numbers below are physical lines (what
`record_ref` stores).

## Hand-made rows

- `Empresas.csv` line 14: second row of 98990011 (duplicate base).
- `Empresas.csv` line 31: **malformed**, 6 columns instead of 7.
- `Socios.csv` line 39: **malformed**, stray quote inside a quoted name.
- `Socios.csv` line 40: **malformed**, empty `cnpj_basico`.
- `Socios.csv` line 41: **malformed**, 12 columns instead of 11.
- `Socios.csv` lines 23 and 24: entry dates `00000000` and empty, and a NUL
  byte in a name. These are quirks of real files, not malformed rows: they
  load (valid_from NULL, NUL removed).

So a full load reads 104 records (31 + 30 + 43) and skips 4.

## How it was made

Generated by a small script from the structure of the 2026-10 files (column
order, quoting, masks such as `***123456**` and `***000000**`, partner types
1/2/3, foreign partners without document, attorneys of foreign partners,
qualification codes). No row was copied from the real files except Banco do
Brasil's Empresas row.
